tagline: From Lost Trail Pass up the River of No Return.
intro: US 93 comes over Lost Trail Pass from Montana at about 7,000 feet and drops with the North Fork of the Salmon to the town of North Fork, where the main river comes up from the south and turns almost square to the west. The byway follows it upstream instead, south through Salmon and Challis.

This is the River of No Return, the longest undammed river in the lower 48 states. Past Challis, Idaho 75 turns west up the river past Clayton, and the Sawtooths come into full view as the road drops into Stanley.
season: Visit Idaho gives April to November as the best weather for travel, and July to October for the back country.

moments.title: North Fork
moments.text: Lewis and Clark are believed to have taken on their guide Toby near here, and he then got them lost crossing into Montana, which is how Lost Trail Pass got its name.

moments.title: Clayton
moments.text: Founded in 1881 as a smelter site for the mines, Clayton counted 10 people at the 2020 census on a hundredth of a square mile, the smallest incorporated city in Idaho.

moments.title: Custer
moments.text: Up the Yankee Fork, the ghost town of Custer sits at 6,470 feet, mostly inside the Land of the Yankee Fork State Park, with seven buildings left that still count as historic.
